<!-- generated from skills/accessibility-i18n/rtl-layouts/SKILL.md (bundle form) -->

# rtl-layouts

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D13 Accessibility & i18n (AC)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** "Internationalization Best Practices: Handling Right-to-left Scripts in HTML", W3C — https://www.w3.org/International/geo/html-tech/tech-bidi.html ; CSS Logical Properties and Values, W3C (via MDN) — https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_logical_properties_and_values
- **Depends on:** internationalization (supplies correct `lang`/`dir` metadata and flexible containers)
- **Feeds into:** localization-workflow (RTL renders are part of its in-context review), wcag (mirrored focus order and reading order feed conformance)

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** Building or reviewing any layout that must serve a right-to-left locale (Arabic, Urdu, Persian, Hebrew) — setting document direction, writing directional CSS, deciding which icons and components flip, isolating embedded LTR content, and running the per-script RTL visual QA pass.
- **Do NOT use when:** Extracting strings, wiring ICU/`Intl` formatting, or setting `lang` (internationalization), running the translation pipeline and its review states (localization-workflow), or judging general WCAG conformance (wcag, accessibility-audit).

## Rules

1. **AC-161 — Direction is declared on the root, never faked or inferred.** Every RTL locale is served with `dir="rtl"` on the document root element, set from the locale's metadata. Direction is never inferred from `lang` by hand-rolled code, never guessed from text content, and never simulated by transforming an LTR layout.
2. **AC-162 — Directional layout uses CSS logical properties only.** Spacing, positioning, borders, radii, and alignment are written as `margin-inline-start`, `padding-inline`, `inset-inline-start`, `border-start-start-radius`, `text-align: start`, and their siblings, so one stylesheet serves both directions and flipping `dir` flips the layout. A physical directional property in component code is a defect.
3. **AC-163 — Flexbox and grid are left to follow direction.** Flex rows and grid inline axes already run in the inline direction; no `row-reverse`, manual `order` shuffling, or direction-detection JavaScript is added to compensate for physical CSS elsewhere — the physical CSS is fixed instead.
4. **AC-164 — What mirrors is decided once, in the design system.** Navigation order, breadcrumb order, progress indicators, pagination, back/forward chevrons, directional flow diagrams, and media-player progress follow the inline direction. The flip/no-flip decision for every icon and component class lives in one design-system list, not in per-screen judgment calls.
5. **AC-165 — Semantic direction never flips.** Clocks and time representations, chart and graph axes tied to data conventions, logos and brand marks, phone keypads, and the media content itself (photos, video) are never mirrored. Play icons are decided once in the tokens per AC-164, not per screen.
6. **AC-166 — Embedded opposite-direction runs are isolated.** An English product name, number, price, or code fragment inside an RTL sentence is wrapped in `<bdi>`, an inline element with an explicit `dir`, or Unicode isolate characters (U+2066–U+2069), so the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm places numbers and punctuation on the correct side.
7. **AC-167 — Inherently LTR content stays LTR.** Code blocks, URLs, email addresses, and phone numbers inside an RTL page render with `dir="ltr"` (and `unicode-bidi: isolate` where they sit inside RTL text), so they read and select in their native order.
8. **AC-168 — Scroll regions, carousels, and sliders start at inline-start.** Horizontal scroll regions begin scrolled to the inline-start edge, carousel advance follows the inline direction, slider value increases toward inline-end, and the scrollbar sits where the platform places it for the document direction — none of these is hard-coded to the left.
9. **AC-169 — Text truncation and alignment follow the logical end.** Body text aligns to `start`; truncation clips at the logical end of the line with the ellipsis there. A deliberate exception (centered display type, justified legal text) is recorded in the design system, not improvised per component.
10. **AC-170 — Numbers and dates are formatted, never hand-reversed.** Digits use the locale's CLDR numbering system as decided per locale, and dates render through `Intl.DateTimeFormat` for the RTL locale. A date or number string is never reversed, reordered, or re-punctuated by string manipulation to "look RTL".
11. **AC-171 — RTL QA is per script, with real text.** Each target script is checked with real content in that script: Arabic (Naskh) passing does not certify Urdu — Nastaliq has far taller line boxes, so line-height, clipping, and truncation are verified separately for Nastaliq, and again for Persian and Hebrew where targeted.
12. **AC-172 — Charts, maps, and diagrams are individually reviewed in RTL.** No chart, map, or annotated diagram ships in an RTL locale until a human has reviewed its RTL render: axis and legend order, label placement, and annotation direction are checked against the data conventions in AC-165.

## BAN list

- **BAN-AC-081 — Physical directional CSS in component code.** Banned: `margin-left`, `padding-right`, `left: 0`, `float: left`, `text-align: right` used to position or align layout in a component. Defeats: DET-UX-023. Instead: the same layout in logical properties (`margin-inline-start: auto`, `inset-inline-start: 0`, `text-align: start`) mirrors automatically when `dir` flips. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AC-082 — Mirroring faked with transforms.** Banned: `transform: scaleX(-1)` (or a flipped duplicate stylesheet) applied to a container or page to simulate RTL. Defeats: DET-VIS-037. Instead: set `dir="rtl"` on the root and build on logical properties (AC-161, AC-162) so content, focus order, and reading order all follow direction. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AC-083 — Un-isolated embedded LTR run in RTL text.** Banned: interpolating a Latin-script product name, number, or price directly into an RTL string with no `<bdi>`, inline `dir`, or Unicode isolate. Defeats: DET-NONE — no DET parameter names this signal; pattern owned by this skill. Instead: the interpolated value is isolated — `<bdi>Pro Max 12</bdi>` — so the bidi algorithm orders the sentence around it correctly. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AC-084 — Blanket-flipping icons and media.** Banned: a global rule such as `[dir="rtl"] svg { transform: scaleX(-1) }` or flipping every icon, logo, and image in RTL. Defeats: DET-UX-015. Instead: only the directional icons on the design-system flip list (AC-164) flip, via a named utility or token; semantic icons, logos, and media never do (AC-165). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AC-085 — Fixed line-height or height tuned to Latin/Arabic text shipped for Nastaliq.** Banned: shipping an Urdu (or any new-script) locale with line-height, fixed-height headings, or single-line truncation carried over from the LTR or Arabic build without a per-script render check. Defeats: DET-VIS-039. Instead: line-height and container heights are verified per script with real Urdu text (AC-171) and fixed heights on text containers are removed or raised until nothing clips. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-AC-081 — Physical-property scan.** Verifies: AC-162, AC-163. Check: run stylelint with a logical-properties rule set (e.g. `stylelint-use-logical-spec` / `liberty/use-logical-spec`) over all component CSS, plus `grep -rnE "(margin|padding)-(left|right)|(^|[^-])(left|right)\s*:|float:\s*(left|right)|text-align:\s*(left|right)" src/ --include='*.css'` as a backstop. Pass: zero findings outside the recorded exception list (e.g. print stylesheets). Fail: block shipment; convert each finding to its logical equivalent and re-run. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AC-082 — RTL render pass.** Verifies: AC-161, AC-164, AC-168, AC-169. Check: with the browser/Playwright, load every key template in an RTL locale and assert `document.documentElement.dir === "rtl"`, `document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= window.innerWidth` (no page-level horizontal overflow), and screenshot each template beside its LTR counterpart for the human diff review. Pass: all assertions hold and a reviewer has signed the LTR/RTL screenshot diff set, including icon flips and scroll-region start positions. Fail: block shipment for that locale; fix and re-render. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AC-083 — Bidi test-string check.** Verifies: AC-166, AC-167, AC-170. Check: render the agreed bidi test set — mixed Arabic/English/number strings, a price with currency, a phone number, a URL, and a code snippet — on the data-dense screens (product, checkout, account) and inspect each render against the expected ordering recorded in the test file. Pass: every test string renders with numbers, punctuation, and embedded LTR runs on the correct side, and code/URL/phone render LTR. Fail: block shipment; add or fix the isolation and re-render. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AC-084 — Per-script visual QA.** Verifies: AC-171, AC-172. Check: for each targeted script beyond the first RTL script (Urdu/Nastaliq, Persian, Hebrew as applicable), screenshot the key templates with real content in that script; a reviewer checks line-height, clipping, truncation direction, and every chart/map/diagram render individually. Pass: signed checklist per script with zero clipped or overflowing text blocks and every chart reviewed. Fail: block shipment for that locale only; the Arabic pass does not substitute. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AC-085 — Icon flip-list conformance.** Verifies: AC-164, AC-165. Check: diff the set of icons flipped in the RTL render (from the G-AC-082 screenshots) against the design-system flip list; grep the codebase for blanket flip rules (`scaleX(-1)` on icon or container selectors). Pass: flipped set matches the list exactly and no blanket flip rule exists. Fail: block shipment; correct the icon utility or the list — in the design system, not per screen. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Flip the document, not the stylesheet: `dir="rtl"` plus logical properties, and mirroring is automatic.
- Physical left/right in a component is a defect, not a style choice.
- Directional icons flip; clocks, charts, logos, and media never do — the list lives in the design system.
- Isolate every embedded run: numbers, names, code, and URLs keep their own direction inside RTL text.
- Arabic passing does not certify Urdu — Nastaliq gets its own visual QA.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every RTL locale serves `dir="rtl"` on the root from locale metadata; no transform-based mirroring exists anywhere.
- [ ] G-AC-081 physical-property scan is clean outside the recorded exception list.
- [ ] G-AC-082 RTL render pass: correct `dir`, zero page-level horizontal overflow, screenshot diff set human-reviewed.
- [ ] Icon and component flips match the design-system flip list exactly — G-AC-085; clocks, charts, logos, and media unflipped.
- [ ] Bidi test strings render with correct ordering on data-dense screens, and code/URLs/phone numbers render LTR — G-AC-083.
- [ ] Scroll regions, carousels, and sliders start at inline-start and advance in the inline direction.
- [ ] Each additional script (Urdu/Nastaliq, Persian, Hebrew) has its own signed visual QA, including every chart and map — G-AC-084.

<!-- generated from skills/accessibility-i18n/screen-readers/SKILL.md (bundle form) -->

# screen-readers

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D13 Accessibility & i18n (AC)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** ARIA Authoring Practices Guide (APG), W3C — https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/ ; WCAG 2.2, W3C — https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/
- **Depends on:** wcag (name/role/value and status-message criteria), accessibility-audit (its smoke-test pass consumes this skill's matrix)
- **Feeds into:** accessibility-testing, keyboard-accessibility, inclusive-copy

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** Building or reviewing anything a screen-reader user must operate or understand — forms, custom widgets, dynamic updates, data tables, navigation — and when running the screen-reader test pass for a release.
- **Do NOT use when:** The defect is purely visual (contrast, focus visibility — wcag / keyboard-accessibility), the question is which law applies (accessibility-law), or the work is a full conformance evaluation (accessibility-audit runs this skill's test matrix as one of its passes).

## Rules

1. **AC-041 — Native semantics first; ARIA is the last resort.** Use the native HTML element for every control and structure (`<button>`, `<nav>`, `<table>`, `<label>`). Add ARIA only where no native element expresses the widget, per the first rule of ARIA use: no ARIA is better than bad ARIA. A role bolted onto a `<div>` is a defect until the full APG pattern (AC-046) is implemented.
2. **AC-042 — Every interactive element has an accessible name that matches its visible label.** The computed accessible name must contain the visible text label (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name), so speech-input and screen-reader users refer to the same control by the same words. Icon-only controls get a name from `aria-label` or visually hidden text that states the action ("Close dialog", not "X").
3. **AC-043 — Headings are a navigation outline, not font sizing.** Headings nest in logical order without skipped levels, each heading text describes the section it opens, and visual size is set with CSS. Screen-reader users navigate by the heading list; an outline that reads as nonsense is a failed page even if it looks right.
4. **AC-044 — Landmarks are few and labeled when repeated.** One `<main>`, one `<nav>` per navigation region; when a landmark type repeats (two `<nav>`s, multiple `<section>`s with `aria-label`), each instance carries a distinct accessible name so the landmark list is usable.
5. **AC-045 — Images: real alt text or empty alt, never a file name.** Informative images get alt text conveying the information the image carries in context; purely decorative images get `alt=""` so they are skipped. File names ("IMG_2043.jpg"), "image", and redundant phrases ("image of") fail this rule.
6. **AC-046 — Custom widgets implement the APG pattern exactly or are replaced.** A custom tabs, menu, combobox, or grid ships with the APG roles, states, properties, and full keyboard model for that pattern — all of it, not the visible half. If the team cannot implement the whole pattern, the widget is rebuilt on native elements.
7. **AC-047 — Dynamic changes are announced by live regions, politely by default.** Status changes (save confirmations, cart totals, step changes, toasts) go through an `aria-live="polite"` region (WCAG 4.1.3); `assertive` is reserved for errors that block the current task. Announcements never move focus — the user hears the change and stays where they are.
8. **AC-048 — Reading order and focus order match the visual order.** DOM order is the single source of sequence: content reads in the same order it is seen, and no CSS (`order`, absolute positioning, grid placement) reorders meaning visually without the DOM agreeing. Multi-column visual layouts built from a scrambled DOM fail this rule.
9. **AC-049 — Data tables use real table semantics with header association.** Data tables are `<table>` markup with `<th>` header cells and `scope` (or `headers`/`id` for complex tables), so a cell is announced with its row and column headers. Layout tables and div-grids presenting tabular data are prohibited; a genuine grid widget follows the APG grid pattern instead.
10. **AC-050 — Language is declared so pronunciation is right.** The document carries a correct BCP 47 `lang`, and any in-page language change is wrapped with its own `lang` (WCAG 3.1.1, 3.1.2). A screen reader pronouncing French text with English rules is a markup defect, not a user problem.
11. **AC-051 — Test in a fixed screen-reader matrix, navigating the way users navigate.** The project fixes its matrix in writing (department default: NVDA + Chrome and JAWS + Chrome on Windows, VoiceOver + Safari on macOS and iOS, TalkBack + Chrome on Android) and records the combinations and date per journey. Testers move by headings, landmarks, link lists, and form-control lists — not only by linear reading — because that is how screen-reader users actually navigate. Untested combinations are stated residual risk, never implied coverage.
12. **AC-052 — Form state is programmatic, not visual.** Required fields expose their required state, invalid fields set `aria-invalid="true"`, and each field's error text and instructions are associated with `aria-describedby`, so the error is announced with the field when the user reaches it — not painted red somewhere on the page.

## BAN list

- **BAN-AC-021 — Clickable divs and spans as controls.** Banned: `<div>`/`<span>` elements with click handlers acting as buttons, links, or tabs, with no role, accessible name, or keyboard path. Defeats: DET-NONE — no DET parameter names this signal; pattern owned by this skill. Instead: use a native `<button>` (or the full APG tabs pattern with `role="tablist"`, arrow-key model, and `aria-selected`). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AC-022 — Placeholder text as the only label.** Banned: form fields labeled only by placeholder text that vanishes on typing. Defeats: DET-UX-022. Instead: give every field a persistent visible `<label>` (or `aria-label` where a visible label is genuinely impossible) and let the placeholder show a format example only. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AC-023 — Silent dynamic changes.** Banned: content that changes on screen — success toasts, totals, step indicators, filtered results — with no live-region announcement, so the change exists only visually. Defeats: DET-UX-011. Instead: route the confirmation through an `aria-live="polite"` status region that announces "Profile saved" without moving focus (AC-047). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AC-024 — Focus dropped to the document top.** Banned: closing a dialog, submitting a form, or changing views in a way that resets focus and the reading position to the top of the document (or nowhere). Defeats: DET-UX-017. Instead: return focus to the control that opened the dialog, and on view change move focus to the new view's heading (AC-048). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AC-025 — Errors announced visually only.** Banned: validation errors shown as red borders or a distant error banner while the field itself carries no programmatic error state or associated message. Defeats: DET-UX-005. Instead: set `aria-invalid="true"` on the field and associate the specific error text with `aria-describedby`, with a polite/assertive announcement per AC-047 and AC-052. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-AC-021 — Automated name/role scan in CI.** Verifies: AC-041, AC-042, AC-045, AC-052. Check: run `npx @axe-core/cli <each key URL> --tags wcag2a,wcag2aa,wcag22aa` in CI (or the project's axe-core job) and fail the build on `button-name`, `link-name`, `label`, `image-alt`, and `aria-required-attr` violations. Pass: zero violations of those rules on every key template. Fail: block merge. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AC-022 — Accessibility-tree name/role assertion.** Verifies: AC-042, AC-044, AC-049. Check: scripted pass over the rendered accessibility tree of each key page (e.g. Playwright's accessibility snapshot): assert every interactive node has a non-empty accessible name and a valid role, repeated landmarks have distinct names, and every data-table cell resolves to at least one header. Pass: zero unnamed interactive nodes, zero unlabeled repeated landmarks, zero headerless data cells. Fail: block release. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AC-023 — Screen-reader smoke pass on primary journeys.** Verifies: AC-043, AC-048, AC-051. Check: manual pass — execute each primary journey in at least one desktop (NVDA + Chrome) and one mobile (VoiceOver + Safari or TalkBack + Chrome) combination from the project's fixed matrix, navigating by headings, landmarks, and form controls; log pass/fail per journey with the AT/browser versions and date. Pass: every primary journey completable end to end in both combinations, with names, roles, and order as designed. Fail: block release. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AC-024 — Live-region announcement test.** Verifies: AC-047, AC-052. Check: with a screen reader running, trigger each dynamic change in the primary journeys (save, add-to-cart, step advance, a blocking validation error, a failed submit) and record what is announced and where focus sits afterward. Pass: every change is announced by the correct live region and focus never moves on a status announcement. Fail: block release. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AC-025 — Heading and landmark outline review.** Verifies: AC-043, AC-044. Check: extract the heading outline and landmark list for each key template (headings-map tool or the screen reader's headings/landmarks dialogs during G-AC-023) and read them as a standalone table of contents. Pass: the outline alone describes the page's structure accurately, with no skipped levels and no heading whose text is styling noise ("Welcome!", "Section 2"). Fail: block release. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Native element first; ARIA only where HTML runs out.
- No name, no control — if it can't be announced, it doesn't exist.
- Headings are the table of contents; write them like one.
- Changes speak politely; only blocking errors interrupt.
- DOM order is reading order — never let CSS tell a different story.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every interactive element has an accessible name containing its visible label (AC-042).
- [ ] No clickable div/span controls remain; custom widgets implement the full APG pattern (AC-041, AC-046).
- [ ] Heading outline reads as an accurate table of contents with no skipped levels (AC-043, G-AC-025).
- [ ] All informative images have real alt text; decorative images have `alt=""` (AC-045).
- [ ] Every dynamic change is announced by a live region without moving focus (AC-047, G-AC-024).
- [ ] Form errors are programmatic: `aria-invalid` plus `aria-describedby` error text (AC-052).
- [ ] Primary journeys passed in one desktop and one mobile matrix combination, versions and date recorded (AC-051, G-AC-023).

# wcag

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D13 Accessibility & i18n (AC)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** WCAG 2.2, W3C — https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/ ; "What's New in WCAG 2.2", W3C WAI — https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/wcag/new-in-22/
- **Depends on:** none (this skill fixes the conformance target every other D13 skill builds or tests against)
- **Feeds into:** accessibility-audit, keyboard-accessibility, screen-readers, accessibility-law, reduced-motion, inclusive-copy

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** Building or changing any interface that must conform — this skill is the conformance discipline itself: how each WCAG criterion is met by construction in design tokens, markup, and interaction code, at the project's fixed target of WCAG 2.2 Level AA.
- **Do NOT use when:** Running an evaluation and producing findings (that is accessibility-audit — it audits against the target this skill sets), mapping laws to a pinned version (accessibility-law), or deep work owned by a sibling skill (keyboard-accessibility, screen-readers, reduced-motion). This skill states the criteria-level requirements those skills implement in detail.

## Rules

1. **AC-021 — Fix the target in writing before build.** Every project records its target as "WCAG 2.2 Level AA" in its project files before interface work starts. Where a contract or law pins an older version (EN 301 549/EAA pins 2.1 AA; Section 508 pins 2.0 AA), the pin is recorded alongside; building to 2.2 AA satisfies the older pins in almost every case, because 2.2 only removes the obsolete 4.1.1 Parsing. Claims are always stated against a named version and level — never bare "WCAG compliant."
2. **AC-022 — Contrast floors, computed from the actual palette.** Normal text ≥4.5:1 (1.4.3); large text ≥3:1 (1.4.3); UI component boundaries and meaningful graphics ≥3:1 against adjacent colors (1.4.11). Ratios are computed from the real token values and re-checked in every state (hover, focus, disabled-looking, placeholder, error) — never eyeballed from a design mock.
3. **AC-023 — Color is never the only carrier of meaning (1.4.1).** Every state or distinction shown in color (error, success, required, chart series, selected) is paired with a redundant cue: text, icon, pattern, or position. If a screen still reads correctly in grayscale, this rule passes.
4. **AC-024 — Focus is visible and never fully hidden.** Every interactive element shows a visible focus indicator (2.4.7), and a focused component is never entirely obscured by author-created content such as sticky headers, cookie banners, or chat widgets (2.4.11). Sticky chrome ships with `scroll-margin` (or equivalent) sized so focused elements clear it.
5. **AC-025 — Pointer targets meet the size floor.** Targets are at least 24×24 CSS px, or have equivalent spacing so a 24px circle centered on the target does not overlap another target (2.5.8). Where space allows, the design target stays in the 44px class; the 2.5.8 floor is a minimum, not a goal.
6. **AC-026 — Everything is keyboard-operable, in logical order, with no traps.** All functionality works by keyboard alone (2.1.1); focus can always move on or out of every component (2.1.2); focus order follows the visual and reading order (2.4.3) with no positive `tabindex` values. Custom widgets follow the sibling keyboard-accessibility skill's APG models.
7. **AC-027 — Name, role, and value are programmatic; status is announced.** Every component exposes its name, role, value, and state to assistive technology (4.1.2) — native HTML elements first, ARIA only where HTML has no equivalent. Status messages (toasts, result counts, save confirmations) are announced via live regions without moving focus (4.1.3).
8. **AC-028 — Text alternatives and persistent labels.** Informative images carry real alt text and decorative images carry `alt=""` (1.1.1) — never a file name. Every form field has a persistent, programmatically associated visible label (1.3.1, 3.3.2); a placeholder may show a format example only. A control's accessible name matches or contains its visible label (2.5.3).
9. **AC-029 — The 2.2 interaction additions are built in.** Every dragging movement has a single-pointer alternative that needs no path-based gesture (2.5.7). Authentication offers a path with no cognitive-function test as the only option — no memorized codes, puzzles, or blocked paste (3.3.8).
10. **AC-030 — Help is consistent and entry is never redundant.** Help mechanisms (contact link, chat, help page) appear in the same relative order on every page that has them (3.2.6). Information the user already gave in the same process is pre-filled or selectable, never re-typed, except where re-entry is essential or security-required (3.3.7).
11. **AC-031 — Conformance is inherited from the design system.** Design tokens are mapped to the criteria they satisfy: each text/background pair to 1.4.3/1.4.11, each target-size token to 2.5.8, each focus style to 2.4.7/2.4.11. A component built entirely from mapped tokens inherits its conformance; a token change re-triggers the mapping check for every criterion that token serves.
12. **AC-032 — Claims are per criterion, per full page, per complete process.** Conformance applies to full pages and complete processes (a checkout fails if step 3 fails), using only accessibility-supported technologies, with non-interference from any non-conforming content on the page. Results are reported per criterion — never as a blanket claim that a page or product "is accessible."

## BAN list

- **BAN-AC-011 — Focus outline removed for looks.** Banned: `outline: none` (or an equivalent reset) on interactive elements with no equal-or-better focus indicator replacing it. Defeats: DET-UX-018. Instead: keep a designed `:focus-visible` indicator on every interactive element, styled from the mapped focus token (AC-024, AC-031). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AC-012 — Color-only state.** Banned: conveying error, success, required, or selection state by color change alone, with no text, icon, or position cue. Defeats: DET-UX-021. Instead: pair every color signal with a redundant cue — an error icon plus a text message naming the problem (AC-023). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AC-013 — Placeholder as the only label.** Banned: a form field whose sole label is placeholder text that disappears on input. Defeats: DET-UX-022. Instead: give every field a persistent visible `<label>`; use the placeholder, if at all, for a format example such as "MM / YY" (AC-028). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-AC-014 — Sub-floor pointer targets.** Banned: shipping standalone interactive targets smaller than 24×24 CSS px without the 2.5.8 spacing exception. Defeats: DET-UX-019. Instead: size targets to at least 24×24 CSS px (44px class where space allows) or space them so the 24px circles do not overlap (AC-025). Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-AC-015 — Overlay widget claimed as conformance.** Banned: installing a third-party "accessibility overlay" or toolbar and treating any criterion as met because of it, instead of fixing the underlying code. Defeats: DET-NONE — no DET parameter names this signal; pattern owned by this skill. Instead: fix the code and tokens so the criterion is met by construction and verified by the gates below; an overlay changes nothing about the rendered page for users who never open it. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-AC-011 — Palette contrast computed by script.** Verifies: AC-022, AC-031. Check: run the project contrast script (e.g. `node scripts/check-contrast.mjs design-tokens.json`), which parses every text/background and component-boundary token pair — including hover, focus, placeholder, and error states — and computes the WCAG ratio from the actual hex values. Pass: every normal-text pair ≥4.5:1, every large-text and non-text pair ≥3:1, zero pairs skipped. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AC-012 — Automated criterion rules pass in CI.** Verifies: AC-027, AC-028. Check: run axe-core in CI over the changed screens (`npx @axe-core/cli <changed URLs>` or the project CI job) and confirm the rules mapped to 4.1.2, 1.1.1, and label criteria report zero violations. Manual form (tool-form substitution): where no browser or axe-core runtime is available, perform the G-AC-015 criterion checklist by hand for the criteria mapped to 4.1.2, 1.1.1, and labels — inspect each changed screen's name/role/value exposure (AC-027), text alternatives, and label association (AC-028) in the accessibility tree and the source — and record it in progress.md as a tool-form substitution for this gate; the automated run remains required wherever tooling exists. Pass: zero violations on the mapped rule set (automated) or zero unmet criteria under the manual form. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AC-013 — Focus spot-verification on changed screens.** Verifies: AC-024, AC-026. Check: manual pass — Tab through every changed screen; at each stop confirm the indicator is visible and not entirely covered by sticky headers, banners, or widgets; confirm focus enters and leaves every component (no trap) in reading order. Pass: every stop identifiable, none obscured, none trapped. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AC-014 — Target sizes measured.** Verifies: AC-025. Check: measure the rendered bounding boxes of all standalone interactive elements on changed screens (DevTools or a Playwright bounding-box script). Pass: every target ≥24×24 CSS px, or its 24px centered circle overlaps no other target. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-AC-015 — Per-release criterion checklist for changed screens.** Verifies: AC-021, AC-032. Check: open the release checklist; for each changed screen, confirm every criterion its changes touch is marked met / not met with the verifying method named (script, CI, or manual pass). Pass: zero unmarked affected criteria, and the target line still reads "WCAG 2.2 Level AA" (or the recorded pinned version). Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Target is named: WCAG 2.2 AA, in writing, before build.
- Contrast is computed from real tokens — never eyeballed.
- Focus visible, focus never fully hidden.
- 24×24 minimum; 44 is the design habit.
- Conformance is per criterion, by construction — never by overlay.

## Checklist

- [ ] Project files record the target "WCAG 2.2 Level AA" plus any law/contract pin (AC-021).
- [ ] Contrast script passes on all token pairs in all states (G-AC-011).
- [ ] No state is carried by color alone anywhere in the changed screens (AC-023).
- [ ] Keyboard walk of changed screens: visible focus at every stop, none obscured, none trapped (G-AC-013).
- [ ] All targets measured at ≥24×24 CSS px or spacing-equivalent (G-AC-014).
- [ ] Every field has a persistent label; every informative image has real alt text (AC-028).
- [ ] Drag actions have a single-pointer alternative; login has a non-cognitive-test path (AC-029).
- [ ] Release checklist marks every affected criterion with its verifying method (G-AC-015).
